issues.legal_issue: Residence anywhere within the relevant village panchayat satisfies an allotment guideline requiring residence in the village where the land is situated.
material_facts: The applicants claimed to live in villages within the same panchayat as the land.
The panchayat comprised several villages, and residents of villages other than the village where the land was located had also been accommodated or proposed for allotment.

The administration’s residence criterion was a guideline, and the authorities had been unable to finalise allotments because of the objection that applicants did not reside in the particular village where the land was situated.
issues.conclusion: Residence within the panchayat satisfies the residence requirement; applicants must establish that residence to the authorities, for example through ration cards, voters lists, or other relevant material.
issues.legal_principle: An administrative guideline is not inflexible where a modest adjustment is needed to fulfil its purpose of providing accommodation to homeless persons in economically backward classes. Residence anywhere within the relevant panchayat may satisfy a guideline framed by reference to the village, while the other stated eligibility criteria remain applicable. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.allotment_eligibility_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether applicants qualify for an allotment of residential land.
predicates.applicants_live_within_same_panchayat: The applicants reside in villages within the panchayat that includes the village where the land is situated.

issues.definition: When an allotment eligibility dispute concerns applicants who live within the relevant panchayat, their panchayat residence satisfies the residence requirement.

issues.legal_issue: Land proposed for residential allotment to underprivileged and economically disadvantaged persons should not be subjected to acquisition in the circumstances stated.
material_facts: The land was vested in the village body.

The village body had resolved to allot the land for residential purposes to persons described as members of Scheduled Castes belonging to the economically backward section and lacking residential accommodation.
An acquisition notification had been issued in respect of the land.
The applicants sought to quash the acquisition in constitutional writ petitions.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition proceedings were quashed because the land was proposed to be used to house members of an underprivileged and economically backward section of the community.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no reason to subject the land to acquisition, particularly when it was proposed to be used for housing underprivileged and economically backward persons. It quashed the acquisition notification made under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenges_acquisiti: The proceeding is a constitutional writ petition challenging acquisition of land.
predicates.land_is_proposed_for_housing_underprivil: The land is proposed to be used to provide homes for underprivileged and economically disadvantaged people.

issues.definition: When a constitutional writ challenges acquisition of land proposed for housing underprivileged people, the acquisition proceedings are quashed.

issues.legal_issue: Eligible residents of the village where land is situated receive priority for allotment, and the remaining land is allotted under the applicable criteria as interpreted by the Court.
material_facts: The village body had adopted a resolution to allot its land for residential purposes, but the resolution had not been implemented.
The Lieutenant Governor had appointed a committee to examine and implement the resolution.
The administration had criteria addressing existing land or housing, income, residence, and plot size.

The Court held that residence within the panchayat could satisfy the residence criterion and that residents of the village where the land was situated, if eligible under the criteria, should receive priority.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were directed to implement the resolution, give priority to eligible residents of the village where the land was situated, allot remaining land under the criteria as interpreted by the Court, and complete allotment within three months of communication of the order to the Lieutenant Governor.
issues.legal_principle: A village-body allotment resolution should be implemented according to the applicable allotment criteria, with eligible residents of the village where the land is located receiving priority. The remaining land is to be allotted under those criteria, applying the Court’s interpretation that residence within the panchayat satisfies the residence requirement. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.writ_seeks_enforcement_of_allotment_reso: The proceeding seeks enforcement of a village body's resolution to allot land for residential purposes.
predicates.allotment_resolution_remains_unimplement: The village body's allotment resolution has not been carried out.
predicates.eligible_local_village_residents_exist: Residents of the village where the land is situated meet the applicable allotment criteria.

issues.definition: When a writ seeks enforcement of an unimplemented residential allotment resolution and eligible residents of the land's village exist, allotment must give those residents priority and apply the criteria to the remaining land.
